_about: Ground truth for intent: what a correct design must be, in the assembled in-use pose with +Z up and z = 0 the build plate. Written from the request text alone, before looking at any model output. Conventions for the checker: 'horizontal' means x or y; horizontal sizes are compared sorted, so 80 x 60 matches 60 x 80; a 'vertical face' has a horizontal normal (+-X or +-Y), a 'horizontal face' has a +-Z normal; roles are case-insensitive regexes over component name + description; nothing below z = 0 is already enforced by the ground audit. Each fact has a plain-English 'says' (what the human gate shows) and a 'check' for code; 'check': null means a human judges it. 'reading': 'interpretation' marks a fact the request does not state outright.
status: DRAFT v2 - drafted by Claude, cross-reviewed by Gemini 3.8 Flash (agy) and DeepSeek v4.1 Flash, each with a blind pass (request text only) and a review pass. Three splits await the user: hinged_box height, phone_stand lip, hair_dryer ring tilt.

laptop_stand_30.says: Two side supports stand upright and parallel, spaced apart
The laptop rests on a surface sloping 30 degrees from horizontal (the supports' top edge, or a deck on them)
A cross bar runs horizontally between the supports and touches both
The cross bar is at the rear (stated), which for a laptop stand is the raised end of the slope

hair_dryer_holder.says: The backplate stands upright, flat against a wall
At least two screw holes pass through the backplate's thickness, into the wall
The cup ring's inner diameter is 90 mm
The ring's axis is vertical (a forward tilt up to 30 degrees is acceptable), so the dryer drops in from above
The ring sits in front of the backplate, away from the wall, and is attached to it

cable_clip.says: The base plate is 40 x 20 mm and lies flat on the desk
A clip arm rises from the base and is attached to it
The clip's cable seat is 6-7 mm across, to hold a 6 mm cable
The snap opening is narrower than the cable, so the cable clicks in and is retained
The cable runs horizontally, along the desk

hinged_box.says: Two parts: a body and a separate lid. No hinge - the text asks for a separate lid, despite the id
The box is 80 x 60 mm in plan
OPEN: 40 mm is the closed box with the lid (my and DeepSeek's reading) OR the body alone (Gemini: equally valid)
The body is open at the top
The lid sits on top of the body and covers its footprint

pen_holder.says: The square base is 80 x 80 mm and lies flat on the plate
Exactly four upright tubes, open at the top
Each tube has a 20 mm inner diameter
The tubes are 100 mm tall (the tube itself, or to the top of the holder)
The tubes stand on the base, inside its footprint

phone_stand.says: A flat base plate lies on the build plate
The backrest leans back at 65 degrees from horizontal (both reviewers' reading; 65 from vertical would be 25)
The backrest slots INTO the base: its foot sits in a slot below the base's top surface, not just touching it
OPEN: a lip or ledge in front of the backrest stops the phone sliding off (Gemini: essential; not in the request)

shelf_bracket.says: The wall plate stands upright, its long side vertical, 150 mm
The shelf arm runs horizontally, 150 mm (its own length or the bracket's reach from the wall)
The arm is at right angles to the wall plate
The arm joins the upper part of the wall plate (the plate may extend above it for a top screw)
A diagonal gusset joins the wall plate and the arm

pi_case.says: A bottom tray, open at the top, sits on the build plate
The tray's inside is at least 85 x 56 mm, the Pi 4 board (domain knowledge, not in the request)
Four vertical standoffs on the tray floor, inside the tray
The standoffs sit on the Pi 4 hole pattern, 58 x 49 mm centres (domain knowledge)
The lid sits on top of the tray and covers it

spool_holder.says: Two end supports stand upright and parallel, on the build plate
The supports are A-shaped: wider at the foot than at the top
One axle rod, 20 mm in diameter and 60 mm long
The axle runs horizontally between the two supports and touches both
The axle is raised, near the top of the A-frames, so a spool can turn

drawer_unit.says: The outer shell is 100 x 80 mm in plan and 60 mm tall
The shell is open at the front: a vertical face, not the top
The drawer is an open-top box inside the shell
The drawer slides out horizontally through the shell's open face
A pull tab sticks out from the drawer's front, at the shell's opening
